verdict.rationale: USPTO documents that sign-in requires a USPTO.gov account with multifactor authentication plus a one-time identity verification. That verification "can be completed online in less than 15 minutes," with paper verification offered only as an opt-out alternative, so an authorized human can finish the path remotely rather than in person or by mailed PIN. However, the evidence never says what the online verification involves, so it cannot rule out biometric or selfie liveness, and that is the core exclusion in the story. missing for 10: documentation of the online identity-verification method (whether it uses biometric liveness or government-ID selfie checks), the specific MFA factors supported, and independent or hands-on confirmation of the remote flow.
